source_title: New Survival Horror Game is a Hodgepodge of The Forest, Resident Evil, and Dead Space
source_excerpt:
New horror games appear practically every week, and it’s easy to understand why. Not only have horror films experienced a boom in recent years, with young standout directors injecting life into the genre, but two classic game franchises, Resident Evil and Silent Hill, have found their groove once again. Add in some strong remakes for classic games like Dead Space , newer horror franchises like The Forest and Outlast continuing to evolve, and plenty of interesting indie games like Tenebris Somnia , and the genre is arguably in the best place it has ever been. And now, Seep is looking to carve out a place for itself within this busy field of games, borrowing from a wide range of horror gems in the process.
More than practically any other genre, it’s easy to pick out which horror games influenced an indie developer, as monster designs, settings, and horror approaches are extremely distinct. Anomaly-spotting? Exit 8 will immediately come to mind. Live-action cinematics? It will be hard not to think of Alan Wake 2 and its brilliant “Champion of Light” sequence. Seep , however, doesn’t just have one or two clear influences. Three very specific franchises make up its DNA, as the game boasts survival/crafting elements and creature design reminiscent of The Forest, Dead Space -like dismemberment, and Resident Evil’ s careful balance of looting and shopping for items.
FIGHT disturbing monsters inside a spooky forest, dismembering them with every gunshot and each bit of trap damage.
STUDY the creatures to use their behavior and attack patterns to your advantage.
CHOOSE whether to support a militaristic faction or some mystical locals.
CRAFT useful traps using scavenged materials and DISTRACT creatures using a drone companion named Daisy.
SURVIVE by looting and purchasing healing items, ammo, and more.
SEEP 's release date is yet to be announced.
"A gritty, realistic first-person horror experience set in a claustrophobic forest haunted by its former residents. Scavenge for supplies, build traps, and survive as long as you can with your drone, Daisy. Grotesque, relentless monsters stalk the woods, and unfathomable terror seeps into the roots."
Seep’s Approach to Creatures Has Massive Forest Vibes
Aside from being set within a creepy forest at nightfall, Seep takes inspiration from the Forest franchise with its creatures. The lumbering former humans known as Gorehusks resemble the Cannibals players fight in moment-to-moment survival, while a few images have been shown that feature a towering spider-legged creature that looks like an alternate take on the Virginia monster. A huge part of survival in The Forest is studying the different hostiles and learning their attacks, and Seep is no different. Players can either kill an unknown monster (which will take a good bit of ammo) to identify it from its corpse, or watch it from a distance and scan it using the protagonist’s trusty drone, Daisy. Once scanned, players will have useful data to utilize in their next encounter, and the Steam page suggests that certain creatures can even be tricked into fighting other monsters once players know how to approach them.
However, Daisy the drone can do more than just scan spooky beings for the player. It’s also a valid distraction device, zooming in front of the player character if commanded to do so and creating either a visual or audio distraction. Beyond that, Daisy can craft traps like tripwires, looping in the crafting mechanics of The Forest series . Players will need materials so that Daisy can make these traps, though, which they’ll be able to loot out of containers and off of dead bodies. Fortunately, Daisy can even pick up crafting materials and ammo that it spots while exploring, and it can warn players of a threat they may not see coming as well. With so many capabilities, it’s easy to imagine Seep players becoming very reliant on Daisy, which could present some real challenges if the bot is ever knocked out of commission.
Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.
Seep’s Other Horror Influences Are Sprinkled Throughout The Experience
While Seep’s setting, enemies, and crafting are all very Forest-like, there are plenty of Resident Evil vibes to point out as well. There’s more shooting and looting than there is in the Forest series, for example, while some NPCs like Lady Fang double as shopkeepers. With a distinct witchy look and a unique way of speaking, Lady Fang wouldn’t look out of place next to RE4’ s Merchant or Village’ s Duke. However, it won’t always be able to reach her and her stock of healing salves and ammunition, so players (and Daisy) will have to scour the environment carefully. As is often the case in survival horror games , that could mean throwing oneself into the fire in the hopes that they’ll escape with more resources than they had going in.
Alongside some Resident Evil -style inventory management, players can expect to see some major Dead Space elements worked into the formula. For starters, there’s apparently an artifact within the enclosed forest that has transformed the locals into otherworldly monsters, which sounds a whole lot like The Marker and the Necromorphs that it spawned . There’s also a ton of focus placed on dismemberment and sound design. Weapons will be weighty, leaves stepped on will crunch under the protagonist’s boot, and the sounds of each creature will be bone-chilling. Every shot fired will cut up hostiles and reveal organs, which serve as weak spots, and environmental destruction will allow for bold approaches to each encounter.
However, throwing The Forest, Dead Space , and Resident Evil into a blender wouldn’t be enough to make Seep feel truly special, as players could simply play any of its influences instead. Fortunately, it does a few things to stand out. First, it rewards environmental destruction by letting players loot collapsed walls and buildings for extra crafting materials, though the sound of destruction can lure monsters toward the player, creating risk and adding tension. Second, the narrative seems to offer players the choice to help either an advanced, militaristic faction or spiritual locals. The protagonist is specifically referred to as a “half-breed” and is seemingly related to a figure called Captain Redfield (another Resident Evil nod, perhaps), suggesting they have ties to both warring factions that will make a decision harder. Some extra trippy moments can be expected as the story unfolds.
